title: What changes when migrating a Spring Boot / JPA application from MySQL to Oracle: dialect, JDBC driver, identifier generation (auto-increment vs sequences), and schema/type differences?
keyPoints: Change the Hibernate dialect to OracleDialect so Hibernate generates Oracle-flavoured SQL (FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY, sequences, Oracle functions).
Swap the JDBC driver from MySQL Connector/J to Oracle ojdbc and change the URL to jdbc:oracle:thin:@//host:1521/service.
Switch IDENTITY (auto-increment) to SEQUENCE with @SequenceGenerator, which also enables batch inserts as a bonus.
Handle schema/type differences: VARCHAR2, NUMBER(p,s), no native BOOLEAN (use NUMBER(1) converter), empty string equals NULL.
Oracle folds unquoted identifiers to UPPERCASE and is case-sensitive for quoted ones; keep naming consistent.
Run migrations in stages: make the app dialect-agnostic first, then switch, then run full regression against a real Oracle instance.

s1_definition.oneliner: MySQL to Oracle means swapping dialect, driver/URL, switching IDENTITY to SEQUENCE, and handling type differences like VARCHAR2, NUMBER, no native BOOLEAN, and empty-string-is-null.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Dialect change** – switch from a MySQL dialect to OracleDialect so Hibernate generates Oracle SQL (FETCH FIRST for pagination, sequence calls, Oracle functions).
- **Driver/URL change** – swap MySQL Connector/J for Oracle ojdbc and change the URL to jdbc:oracle:thin:@//host:1521/service.
- **Identifier generation** – MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT (IDENTITY) does not exist the same way in Oracle; switch to SEQUENCE with @SequenceGenerator, which also enables batch inserts.
- **Type differences** – VARCHAR2 instead of VARCHAR, NUMBER(p,s) instead of DECIMAL, no native BOOLEAN in older Oracle (use NUMBER(1) converter), CLOB/BLOB for large data.
- **Empty string equals NULL** – Oracle treats '' as NULL, which changes behaviour for NOT NULL columns and equality comparisons.
- **Identifier case** – Oracle folds unquoted identifiers to UPPERCASE; quoted identifiers are case-sensitive.
s1_definition.analogy: Moving National Bank of India's data from one vault manufacturer (MySQL) to another (Oracle) means the lock mechanism is different (driver), the clerk must speak the new vault's dialect of filing instructions (dialect), the way new file numbers are issued changes from a built-in counter to a separate number-dispenser (sequences instead of auto-increment), and some box shapes differ: there is no true yes/no box, text boxes are a different type, and an empty box is treated as if it were missing.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Migrating a JPA application from MySQL to Oracle touches four layers. First the dialect: Rajesh changes Hibernate's dialect to OracleDialect so it generates Oracle SQL with FETCH FIRST for pagination and sequence calls for identifiers. Second the driver and URL: he swaps the MySQL Connector/J for Oracle's ojdbc and changes the JDBC URL format. Third, and this is the biggest code change, identifier generation: MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT with IDENTITY is replaced by SEQUENCE with a @SequenceGenerator and a created Oracle sequence, which as a bonus enables batch inserts that IDENTITY never allowed.

Fourth, the schema and type differences at National Bank of India cause the subtle runtime surprises. VARCHAR becomes VARCHAR2, DECIMAL becomes NUMBER with precision and scale for money, older Oracle has no native BOOLEAN so a Java boolean maps through a converter to NUMBER(1), large text becomes CLOB, and crucially Oracle treats an empty string as NULL. Pankaj audits every NOT NULL varchar column and every comparison against empty strings before migration.

The senior point is that the dialect only fixes Hibernate's generated SQL, not any native SQL the team wrote by hand. Before flipping the dialect, Pankaj audits every native query for MySQL-only constructs, keeps identifier naming consistent because Oracle folds unquoted names to uppercase, and runs the migration in stages with ddl-auto set to validate against a real Oracle instance.

Remember one sentence: MySQL to Oracle means switching dialect, driver, and IDENTITY to SEQUENCE, plus handling VARCHAR2, NUMBER, no BOOLEAN, and empty-string-is-null.
